description: K₃Na(SO₄)₂ crystallizes in the trigonal P̅3m1 space group. There are two inequivalent K sites. In the first K site, K is bonded in a 10-coordinate geometry to ten O atoms. There are a spread of K-O bond distances ranging from 2.59-3.04 Å. In the second K site, K is bonded to twelve O atoms to form distorted KO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share edges with six equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, edges with six equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra, and faces with two equivalent NaO₆ octahedra. There are six shorter (2.89 Å) and six longer (3.27 Å) K-O bond lengths. Na is bonded to six equivalent O atoms to form NaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six equivalent SO₄ tetrahedra and faces with two equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. All Na-O bond lengths are 2.35 Å. S is bonded to four O atoms to form SO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with three equivalent NaO₆ octahedra and edges with three equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 17°. There is one shorter (1.46 Å) and three longer (1.49 Å) S-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to four K, one Na, and one S atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to four K and one S atom.
